findings.rationale: MN's uploaded updates are about 11x the median norm (size-adjusted z about +10) in every round from round 1, while the cosine to the median update swings between positive and negative with no consistent direction (mean cos 0.16, min -0.30). This is the signature of large random noise added to uploads, not a consistent sign-flip or scaling. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.797, CITL 0.005), so this is not label noise or prevalence shift, and the data look fine.

OH's updates are about 12x the median norm (size-adjusted z about +11) from round 1, with cosine to the median swinging between roughly +0.45 and -0.31 across rounds and a mean of only 0.11. This is the same random-noise upload pattern as MN and SC. Local AUC (0.801) and CITL (-0.010) are normal.

SC's updates are about 9x the median norm (size-adjusted z about +11) in every round, with cosine to the median oscillating around zero (mean 0.14, min -0.30). Same random-noise upload signature as MN and OH. Local AUC (0.795) and CITL (-0.024) are within normal range.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed leads with narrower queries. Three clients (MN, OH, SC) show a strong, consistent upload anomaly: update norms roughly 9–12x the median (size-adjusted z about +10 to +11) from round 1, with cosine to the median fluctuating around zero rather than aligning. I read this as large random noise in uploads (explanation_instability), not a consistent sign-flip or scaling attack, and their local performance and calibration are normal. Other leads did not hold up: the negative Sex means for AL, AK and GU were noise (narrower query showed normal 0/1 values); AL's drift, and the GA, WV and NV AgeGroup subgroup outliers, were not reproducible at the available epsilon; the client_performance screen showed no AUC, CITL or prevalence flags, so no label-noise or prevalence-shift findings. Budget is essentially fully spent (0 remaining). Confidence is moderate, since three clients sharing the same signature is at the upper end of 'a few'.
